question: How are models evaluated in this human-machine communication game?

extractive_spans: by training an autocomplete system on 500K randomly sampled sentences from Yelp reviews
evidence: We evaluate our approach by training an autocomplete system on 500K randomly sampled sentences from Yelp reviews BIBREF6 (see Appendix for details). We quantify the efficiency of a communication scheme $(q_{\alpha },p_{\beta })$ by the retention rate of tokens, which is measured as the fraction of tokens that are kept in the keywords. The accuracy of a scheme is measured as the fraction of sentences generated by greedily decoding the model that exactly matches the target sentence.

title: Learning Autocomplete Systems as a Communication Game
answer_short: Based on efficiency (fewest tokens), accuracy (faithful sentence transmission), and interpretability (learnability by humans).
answer_rationale: The evaluation of models in this human-machine communication game is explicitly defined by three criteria: efficiency (using as few tokens as possible), accuracy (transmitting sentences faithfully), and interpretability (being learnable by humans). This is stated in the abstract (Text 1, source_id=2), which also notes that experiments show improved accuracy and time savings under this framework. The approach further supports interpretability by using keywords extracted from source sentences (Text 2, source_id=12), and the communication game structure involves encoding and decoding strategies (Text 3, source_id=10).
